title: Simulations of Social Mechanics and Forces of Uncertainty Within the Corporate Environment: A Methodology for the Professional Training of IT Specialists and the Statistical Aspects of Its Effectiveness
content: (1) Background. Established educational processes often fail to replicate the volatile workflow of the IT industry. A critical challenge lies in preparing students for uncertainty and volatility in labor market conditions. This study develops a gamified methodology designed to foster essential soft skills in future IT specialists. (2) Methods. This paper outlines the methodology and its quantitative performance metrics based on an experiment conducted from 2023 to 2026 at Moscow Polytechnic University. Conventional statistical tools, including Sheppard’s correction, Student's t-test, and Pearson's and Spearman's correlation coefficients, were applied to analyze group dynamics, ranking volatility, and network interaction structures. (3) Results. Game-based ranking pressure successfully disrupts linear academic patterns and activates latent behavioral strategies. This volatile approach completely eliminates the Gaussian normal distribution, creating a discrete, polymodal ranking structure that divides students into polar subclusters. Students resolve the didactic duality between personal gain and team synergy through network self-organization and local symbiotic alliances, while psychological pressure is balanced by voluntary participation and prompt debriefing. (4) Conclusions. The proposed mathematical framework enables continuous monitoring of role structures within student groups. Further development involves cross-institutional transfer of this methodology to regional universities to test the invariance of the identified behavioral patterns.
